questions.q: What does a function with no explicit return statement return in JavaScript?
options: undefined, every time, silently
null
The last value console.log printed
A runtime error is thrown
questions.explain: JavaScript functions implicitly return undefined when no return statement executes — a common source of confusion for beginners.

questions.q: In function greet(name) { return `Hello, ${name}`; }, what is name called, and what is "Ana" called in greet("Ana")?
options: name is the parameter; "Ana" is the argument
name is the argument; "Ana" is the parameter
Both are called arguments
Both are called parameters
questions.explain: A parameter is the placeholder in the function definition; an argument is the actual value passed at the call site.

questions.q: What does a default parameter value do in function greet(name = "friend") {...}?
options: It's used automatically whenever the caller doesn't pass that argument at all
It overrides whatever value the caller passes in, always
It makes the parameter required rather than optional
It has no effect unless explicitly invoked with a special keyword
questions.explain: If the caller omits the argument, the default value fills in; if the caller passes a value, that value is used instead.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between a function declaration and a function expression?
options: A declaration is hoisted and can be called earlier in the file than where it's written; an expression assigned to a variable cannot
A function expression runs faster at runtime than a declaration
Only a function declaration can accept parameters
There is no difference of any kind between the two forms
questions.explain: Hoisting moves function declarations to the top of their scope before the code runs; expressions stored in variables aren't hoisted the same way.

questions.q: In const subtract = function (a, b) { return a - b; };, what kind of function is this?
options: A function expression, stored in a variable
A function declaration
An arrow function
A class method
questions.explain: Assigning an anonymous function to a variable is the classic function expression pattern.
